description.purpose: The colony shell: the outermost of the four composition levels, and the tree everything else is grown into. It is authored under one rule that all four levels repeat in the same words -- A LEVEL OWNS WHAT ITS SIBLINGS MUST SHARE. What every organisation of a colony shares is the capability broker and the control loop, so those two stand here as refs, pinned to exact versions; beside them stands `orgs`, a real but empty container hive. The shell holds no cell of its own, no memory, no model and no state: it routes seven lanes in, nine lanes out, and owns the boundary.
description.use_when: Once per colony, as the first thing an operator instantiates. Everything else arrives afterwards as an organisation instantiated into `./orgs`, and the mutation that grows one draws that organisation's own edges in the same breath. Do not instantiate a second shell into a colony that already has one: two brokers mean two answers to the same question, and two control loops mean two hands on the same params.
description.not_in_scope: No `turn` lane outward: the level declares the UNION of what its occupants emit, minus what a sibling inside consumes itself -- and a member consumes its own turn behind its screen (`./assistants -> ./firewall`), so an exit for it here could never fire. No second vault: `access@2.0.5` carries its own interior one and the standalone `vault` template attests its inbound edges against `params.broker` plus `params.sealed_neighbors`, so a copy at this level would boot locked and inert (ruling Q20, GH #302). No swallowing sink: nothing here accepts a refusal and emits nothing, because the dead-letter queue is the record (ruling Q2, GH #284). No `connect` lane outward: `access` requires that lane to be the ONE edge that reaches a connector cell, and that edge is drawn where the connector stands, not here. No contract on the container: the level declares the transit lanes and its own edges satisfy them from birth (W7-R2). No organisation-level anything -- the shell ships the container, never a tenant. And no slot: the substrate's slot governs an address that does not exist, while `orgs` does exist, so the declaration would have been silent and the `params.ports` it needs would have SEALED this hive.
examples: LANES - the hive path is the address and `hop.route` is the lane; `params.ports` is ABSENT, which is the open state, and no edge from outside is refused by a boundary this level does not draw. in_request and in_invoke reach the broker and both demand a promoted `context.requester`; in_cycle reaches the control loop; in_turn, in_recall, in_brief and in_propose reach the `orgs` container. grant, ack, mutate, answer, reject and error leave the hive path -- `turn` does NOT, because a member consumes its own turn behind its screen. Nothing addresses an occupant by name from outside: the occupants are refs, and their interiors belong to their own templates.

THE TWO REFS - `access@2.0.5` and `steward@2.0.11`, pinned to exact versions rather than named bare. A bare name resolves to the newest version on disk, so a shell that shipped one would silently adopt a new broker the day a bump landed -- which is precisely the drift `registry.template_chain` exists to make visible, not to excuse. The chain a grown node carries reads outermost-first: `meclaw-os` and then the occupant's own template.

THE CONTAINER - `orgs` is a real hive with no children, no edges and no `params` block at all. Real, because #303 forces the same shape one level further down (`channels` must be a node to carry its fan-in edges once) and four levels with one shape beat four levels with three. Empty, because an organisation is instantiated INTO it. Open, because the instantiating mutation draws edges to that organisation and a sealed hive refuses exactly those endpoints. And SILENT, because a contract on an empty hive declares doors that lead nowhere: the level declares the organisation's own lanes instead -- four in, seven out -- and its own eleven edges to and from `./orgs` satisfy the door-and-exit check from birth (W7-R2).

THE STEWARD TALKS TO THE COLONY - since GH #267 the control loop asks `/colony/ledger` for its numbers instead of opening a database it does not own. Two absolute lanes, `./meter` and `./probe` onto that endpoint, travel with the ref: this shell writes no edge for them and must not seal them away. The virtual endpoints are in bounds at every scope, so wrapping the loop one level deeper changes nothing about them.

IT DECIDES NOTHING - nineteen internal edges, every one of them a door or an exit. The shell has no cell, so it cannot compute, refuse or remember. A level that grew one of those would have stopped being a boundary and started being a participant.
